key_insight: The paper explains grokking as a geometry-driven transition in parameter space: optimization first lands on a memorization shell and only later escapes to a core of generalizing solutions.
engineering_relevance: Its scaling laws for learning rate, batch size, and L2 regularization can help practitioners tune training to reduce delayed generalization and better predict when grokking will occur.
method: Characterize Adam with weight shrinkage as inducing a shell–core topology of reachable solutions.
Use stopping-time theory to analyze when trajectories leave the memorization manifold and reach the generalization boundary.
Derive scaling laws for grokking with respect to learning rate, batch size, and L2 regularization.
evidence_signal: The theory is supported by empirical evidence and validated experiments that recover scaling results reported in prior grokking literature.
watch_item: The shell–core explanation is a theoretical abstraction, so its practical accuracy may depend on optimizer choice, model architecture, and the specific training setup.
paper_title: A Stochastic--Geometric Theory of Scaling Laws in Grokking
